analysis: What changed versus Monday's 9:00 AM brief: the rebound not only held, it accelerated into the close — the S&P 500 gained 2.35% Monday, its biggest one-day jump since April, the Dow added 1,104 points (+2.15%) and the Nasdaq +2.74%, with semis +6.85% and the VIX collapsing 22% to 19.92. Overnight the story flipped from relief rally to a rate-hike referendum: Fed Governor Waller's London speech (published 09:00 GMT) made a December hike effectively a done deal in his view — 25bp even if CPI cools, 50bp if core prints 0.3% or more — and December-hike pricing jumped toward 99%. That puts one tenth of a point between a routine hike and an upsized one, and BLS will not publish annual rates for indexes missing October 2025 data, so the monthly core print gets read more closely than usual. Nvidia is steadying (+1.3-1.8% premarket after Monday's -4.27% to a seven-month low) with a new wrinkle: Trump said Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy and that he believes him, with the FBI looking into it — but the board probe still has no timeline and the House Nov 11 reply deadline is tomorrow. Take-Two's quarter was soft (bookings -18%, just under its own guide) yet the stock is up ~3-4% premarket because the GTA VI date held and pre-orders are 'far in excess' of expectations — the launch, not the quarter, is the trade. Sanmina's +19% premarket on a big FY27 guide is the other side of the AI-spending debate: hardware suppliers are still getting paid even as Citi cut US equities and global tech to neutral on crowded AI positioning. Oil's slide below $90 Brent on Trump's Iran comments is a second tailwind into CPI. Signal vs noise: Waller's explicit 0.3% core trigger, the CPI print itself, Sanmina's guide and Take-Two's GTA VI confirmation are signal; the day-to-day NVDA governance headlines are noise until the board or the House briefing produces something concrete; the Anthropic IPO roadshow is real but a next-week pricing story, not a today story.

community_signals.takeaway: Discussion has moved past the letter itself: top threads now debate whether Trump's public 'I believe him' comment and the FBI inquiry change the governance overhang, and a Nov 9 comment notes a Wired report that Huang hired a crisis PR firm before the story broke — the thread's read is that the apology was skillfully handled but the board investigation's open-ended timeline is what keeps the discount on the stock.

headlines.headline: Futures are mixed and mostly flat ahead of the 8:30 AM ET October CPI: as of 5:36 AM ET, S&P 500 futures +0.10%, Dow futures +0.33% and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.22%. The CPI consensus is headline +0.3% m/m (down from September's +0.6%) and core +0.2% (down from +0.3%); annual core is estimated at 2.8% versus 2.6% in September.
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat, wait-and-see tape after Monday's 2.35% surge — the CPI print decides whether the rebound extends or the rate-hike debate takes it back.

headlines.headline: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a London speech on Tuesday that he would support a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting even if October CPI improves, and that a 50bp hike 'should be considered' if core CPI rises 0.3% or more — warning that hiking only 25bp in that case 'would put our credibility at risk.' The 2-year Treasury yield rose 4bp on the remarks and December-hike pricing jumped toward 99%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Waller turned CPI into a referendum on a bigger hike — one tenth of a point in core inflation now separates a routine 25bp from a 50bp move, which is why futures barely moved overnight despite the hawkish tone.

headlines.headline: Nvidia rose 1.3-1.8% in premarket trading, attempting a recovery after falling 4.27% Monday to $178.67, a seven-month low, following reports about CEO Jensen Huang's alleged links to a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. President Trump said Nov 9 that Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy, that he believes him, and that the FBI is looking into it. The board probe has no published timeline; Huang must reply by Nov 11 to House chairmen's request for a closed-door briefing Nov 18. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
headlines.why_it_matters: A tentative bounce after a brutal week (NVDA -11.58% over the past week, 25% below its 52-week high) — but with no board timeline and the House deadline tomorrow, the recovery is fragile and the story is still about governance uncertainty, not fundamentals; the spy claims remain anonymous-source reporting with no public finding.

headlines.headline: Oil kept sliding: Brent crude fell 3.6% and slipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August, and WTI traded around $84.59, down 2.6%, after President Trump said military action against Iran was not needed 'at this point' and that the war was 'effectively over militarily,' easing fears of supply disruption. Brent is down nearly 17% over the past week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cheaper crude eases an inflation input hours before CPI and supports consumers and airlines — a second tailwind behind the equity rebound, though energy names stay under pressure.

headlines.headline: Take-Two reported fiscal Q2 net bookings of $1.60B, down 18% YoY and just under its own $1.62-1.67B guide and the $1.67B analyst estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.00 beat the $0.90 consensus. The stock rose 3-4% premarket: GTA VI is still dated Nov 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, development is complete, pre-orders are 'tracking far in excess' of initial expectations, and full-year net bookings guidance was held at $8.0-8.2B, with the launch quarter guided at $3.35-3.50B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The quarter was soft but nobody is trading the quarter — the GTA VI date holding and pre-orders running ahead of plan is what the stock is reacting to, ten days before launch.

headlines.headline: Sanmina jumped about 19% premarket after reporting fiscal Q4 revenue of $3.86B and non-GAAP EPS of $4.43, and guiding fiscal 2027 revenue to $17.5-19.5B and non-GAAP EPS to $15.50-17.50, both above estimates. Sanmina builds servers and networking gear for data centers. Separately, Citi cut US equities and global tech to neutral from overweight on Nov 9, citing crowded AI positioning.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hardware supplier guiding well above estimates says AI spending is still flowing to the buildout — the counterweight to last week's data-center slowdown fears and to Citi's downgrade of the crowded AI trade.

headlines.headline: Anthropic is expected to formally launch the roadshow for its IPO on Tuesday, with pricing expected next week, setting up one of the biggest IPOs on record. A listing could force other AI heavyweights to compete harder for investor dollars. Separately, CoreWeave reports Q3 results after today's close (call 5:00 PM ET); its shares were up 2.4% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Anthropic listing is the next big AI-capital event and a fresh supply of AI equity for investors to weigh against the megacaps; CoreWeave's print tonight is the nearer test of neocloud demand and debt worries.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.32M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, in line), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Call color: over 60% of new horsepower scheduled for 2027 delivery is contracted (~90% of first-half deliveries); ~$500M order book through 2029; utilization slipped to 92.1% from 94.0%. New filing note: Alps Advisors raised its stake 15.5% in Q3 and now owns ~14.55% of the partnership. Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September. Cross-current today: WTI's slide toward ~$84.59 pressures energy names broadly, though USAC's compression business is fee-based.

watch_next: 8:30 AM ET today: October CPI — headline +0.3% m/m and core +0.2% expected; a core print of 0.3% or more puts Waller's 50bp December hike on the table, while 0.2% or below likely keeps it at 25bp. No official annual rates for indexes missing October 2025 data.
Whether Nvidia's premarket bounce holds — House chairmen's Nov 11 reply deadline for the Nov 18 closed-door briefing is tomorrow; NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
After the close today: CoreWeave (Q3, call 5:00 PM ET) — the neocloud demand/debt test after Sanmina's strong guide; also D-Wave Quantum and Rigetti.
Wed Nov 11: Veterans Day — bond market closed; Thu Nov 12 after close: Cisco and Applied Materials; Fri Nov 13, 8:30 AM ET: October PPI.
Oil: whether Brent holds below $90 and WTI's slide toward the mid-$80s continues to ease the inflation print and support the rally.
